Deceptive Statistics Statistics is one of the powerful technique but sometimes
the way media or politicians present it can be very deceptive. Many time it is
just a mechanism for headline grabber Say ruling party during budget increases
some base essentials tax from 6 to 9%. Now this can be represented in 2 way.
Ruling party might say it as 3 percentage point increase but opposition might
call it out as 50% increase in taxes. Both are right but intensity is
different for normal citizens out there There are also misrepresented
statistics like people calling out python is used 80% and R - 20%. Other tools
like sas as 0%. If we correlate it against the revenue the other company is
making it shows the truth behind it Reason for this post is there have been
cases where individuals have been wrongly jailed of crime due to wrong use of
statistics. Check the post below in first comment where Sally Clark spent 3
years in prison due to wrong statistical information presented until it was
overturned Use statistics wisely and correctly.. hashtag#datascience

post_content:
A Data Scientist without creativity is unquenchable. A data scientist with
creativity is unstoppable. The reason is - if a Data Scientist doesn't have a
creative mind, at every problem he asks others/google those questions or ideas
to tackle those problems. So his questions cannot be quenched.Hence
unquenchable The DS with creativity doesn't have time to execute all his ideas
on feature engineering. So even at 10 PM on Sunday night, he keeps working on
models/insights. Hence unstoppable I wrote this as comment on Suneel Patel
status about the importance of creativity for a data scientist. Putting it
here for wider audience

questions to data scientist in daily stand up call as asked to software
engineers 1) What did you accomplish yesterday? 2) What is expected to be done
today? 3) What obstacles are impeding the progress? 3rd one is completely fine

hashtag#Forbes 30 Under 30 hashtag#Fortune 30 under 30 BW Disrupt 40 under 40
Don't get intimated by these "Under" tags. There was a time when they really
fascinated me. Then came a time when people around me started getting them (
that was the worst ). At one point in time, I started seeing them everywhere:
School reunion, my batchmate have one, got invited for judging a
hashtag#startup hashtag#Competition, expect me both judges were. There came a
time when the guy sitting next to me in a flight was one. Over a period of
time, I realized that it is something which has a lot to do what with the
domain of work rather than your work. The domain/sector which is in the news.
And secondly, how good is your PR Team (not saying that it is like film awards
and can be bought). How your PR team is presenting you in front of the world.
The message if for the students and entrepreneurs: Don't aim for being in that
list, keep your head down and do good work. It will just help you get a good
cover photo for your social media channels, success is not that. Success is
much more than "Under" tags.

post_content:
Ravi Chitloor, chief architect - Data protection of DELL EMC was programming
when he was ten years old! He is about 3 years younger to me as per TOI. I
think, at the age of 10, I knew only radio programs and probably didnt even
know the existence of computers. Forget programming. What I was doing at 10,
remotely related to my profession at this moment was I would go, pick herbs
with Granny, make extracts to help her and see how she works around it.
Basically a healer. I would come back home and try these on my playmates,
friends and poor kids especially on the wounds which were part of our day to
day ups and downs. Observe them heal. I would check them on as well if they
have gotten cured by my trial and error method. Yes before you ask, no
mortalities recorded. I would also dismantle electronic instruments like
clocks, watches, calling bells, sometimes those kerosene or pump stoves
(remember that?), cycles things like that. Was fascinated with the process of
work integration of those tiny things inside. What were you doing at age 10,
which you can remotely connect with your profession?
